overview.description: Pinochle for two players. Melding and trick-taking with 48-card deck; two-player rules (e.g. dummy hand or special deal).

history.origins: Pinochle is derived from bezique and is related to Binokel (Binocle), which developed in Switzerland and South Germany. German immigrants brought Binokel to America in the last quarter of the 19th century, where it was mispronounced and misspelled as pinochle. It became a favorite of American Jewish and Irish immigrants. The two-player form uses the same 48-card deck and follows the same meld-and-trick structure: bidding, melding, then trick play adapted for two hands. During World War I some US cities briefly outlawed pinochle due to anti-German sentiment; it has since regained popularity.
timeline: Late 19th century: Brought to USA by German immigrants as Binokel; name became Pinochle.

setup.deck: 48 cards (two copies of 9, 10, Jack, Queen, King, Ace in each of four suits).
setup.dealing: Deal twelve cards to each player in packets of four; 24 cards remain as stock. In bidding variants, bid winner may declare trump then both lay melds; in classic variant, players draw one card from stock after each of the first twelve tricks and may meld after winning a trick.

rules.objective: Score points via melds and trick-taking; first to reach agreed target (e.g. 1000) wins, or win by making your bid (meld plus trick points).
rules.gameplay: Deal 12 each. Auction: players bid in turn or pass; highest bidder declares trump. Both players lay melds face-up, tally, return cards to hand. Trick play: bid winner leads; must follow suit, must play trump when void in suit; must overtrump when possible in some rules. Counters (A, 10, K) score 10 each; last trick 10. Total 250 trick points per hand.
keyRules: Bid or pass; high bidder names trump.
Meld then tricks; follow suit; trump beats non-trump.
Rank order A 10 K Q J 9; Jack and Queen of trump are highest.

play_card.description: Play one card to the trick; must follow lead suit if possible; if void in suit must play trump if possible; highest card of led suit or highest trump wins trick.
play_card.constraints: Follow suit when able; when void in lead suit, play trump if possible; identical cards rank first-played higher. Trick winner leads next.

draw.reason: This game has no draw-from-stock action.

discard.reason: This game has no discard pile.

pass.description: Pass and drop out of the auction; cannot bid again this round.
pass.constraints: Legal when it is your turn to bid; after passing you are out of the auction.

bid.description: Make a bid (points you predict to make from melds and tricks); highest bidder wins and declares trump.
bid.constraints: Each bid must be higher than the previous; bids in multiples of 10 or 25 depending on house rules.

meld.description: Lay melds face-up for count: runs, marriages, pinochles, arounds, dix; cards are returned to hand after tally.
meld.constraints: Bid winner melds first; then other player. One meld per type per card; same card can count in different meld types.

go_out.reason: This game has no go-out action.

trumpConfig.overtakingRule: Jack of trump and Queen of trump are highest; must follow suit then must overtrump when possible.

trickConfig.leadRestrictions: Bid winner leads first trick; then trick winner leads.

customActions.description: Deal twelve cards to each player in packets of four; 24 cards remain as stock.
customActions.constraints: Dealer acts; deal clockwise starting with player to dealer's left.

engine.deckDescription: A 48-card Pinochle deck: four French suits, each with two copies of 9, 10, Jack, Queen, King, Ace. Two-hand Pinochle uses one pack; players bid, meld, and play tricks; deal and scoring follow the two-player variant rules.
engine.suitDescription: The four French suits (hearts, diamonds, clubs, spades) each have twelve cards. Trump is determined by bid; marriages and melds use suit and rank; in tricks, following suit is required when possible.
engine.rankDescription: Pinochle rank order: 9 low, then 10, Jack, Queen, King, Ace; Jack of trump and Queen of trump are the two highest trumps. Rank sets trick winners and meld values (marriage, run, pinochle, etc.).

notApplicableReasons.shedding: Game is meld and trick-taking; no shedding or going-out empty-hand.

synthesis.shortDescription: Pinochle for two players. Melding and trick-taking with 48-card deck; two-player rules (e.g. dummy hand or special deal).

scoring.description: Meld points (runs, marriages, pinochles, arounds, dix) plus trick points. Counters in tricks: A 10 K worth 10 each; last trick 10; total 250 per hand. Bid winner must make at least bid or score is deducted.
scoring.winCondition: First player to reach agreed target score (e.g. 1000) wins; or high score after agreed number of hands.

penalties.fail_bid: Bid amount subtracted from score; meld may be cancelled for that hand.
